::: {.why}
The last day of phase 1, and the one that decides what you spend the other 338 on: some of these businesses are closed to you by capital, some by latency, and one is not closed at all.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Compute what a 2-and-20 fee structure does to an investor's net return at a gross Sharpe of 1, and say what that implies about the gross return a fund must produce.
- Name the three constraints that decide capacity, and say which one binds first for a strategy trading 500 US large caps daily.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Read one AQR research piece on trend following or on the fee-adjusted value of active management, and note the size of the effect the authors claim rather than the direction.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Fee arithmetic: gross return 10 percent, volatility 10 percent, fees 2 percent management and 20 percent of profits. Compute net return, net volatility and net Sharpe. Then find the gross Sharpe needed to deliver a net Sharpe of 1. Do this once and you will never again be impressed by a gross number.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Write the closing section of the market map: for each of the six businesses from day 1, one sentence on whether you can compete with it and what the binding constraint is. Speed for market making, capital for pod shops, and information for event-driven are the three answers you should reach.
:::
:::
